entities.name: PMID:25441012
observations: Retrospective National Inpatient Sample analysis (2003–2011) comparing 306,438 vascular-surgery patients at safety-net and nonsafety-net public hospitals.
Study included surgery for peripheral arterial disease, carotid stenosis, and nonruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm.
Safety-net hospitals had longer stays and higher hospital charges; adjusted in-hospital mortality was not significantly different.
Unadjusted mortality was higher at safety-net hospitals (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.13–1.46), but the difference disappeared after multivariable adjustment.

entities.name: Safety-net public hospital
observations: In the cited vascular-surgery study, care was associated with significantly longer length of stay and higher hospital charges than at nonsafety-net public hospitals.
Higher crude mortality was explained by adjustment for patient and clinical differences; adjusted mortality was similar.

entities.name: Nonsafety-net public hospital
observations: Comparator hospitals in the cited study had lower length of stay and hospital charges, while adjusted in-hospital mortality did not differ significantly from safety-net hospitals.
